criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies overbroad MAE carve-outs for environmental industry/regulations
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the environmental-services industry and Environmental Laws carve-outs as overbroad because they lack disproportionate-impact qualifiers, and proposes adding such qualifiers to both clauses.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes adding disproportionate impact qualifier to MAE carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing both the environmental-services industry carve-out and the Environmental Laws/regulations carve-out with language excepting changes that disproportionately affect the Company relative to other industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Provides actual revised contract language for MAE definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides draft-ready replacement text for clauses (ii) and (iii) of the MAE definition, expressly adding exceptions where industry or Environmental Law changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Explains rationale — environmental company needs MAE protection
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that the Target is an environmental-services business and that blanket carve-outs for environmental-industry downturns or changes in Environmental Laws would shift the sector-specific risks central to the valuation and diligence to Buyer. It further explains that disproportionate-impact qualifiers are needed to preserve MAE protection for target-specific effects.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies missing interim covenant restricting affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies in Item 3 that Section 6.01's interim covenants lack an affiliate-transaction restriction and proposes requiring Buyer consent for Company transactions with Seller or Seller affiliates between signing and closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes covenant requiring Buyer consent for affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: Item 3 proposes adding Section 6.01(b)(xiv), which prohibits the Company from entering into, renewing, extending, amending, modifying, waiving rights under, terminating, or otherwise altering any agreement or transaction with Seller or any Seller affiliate without Buyer's prior written consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: References the above-market rent to Seller affiliate as rationale
criteria_results.reasoning: In Item 3, the memorandum uses Schedule 4.21’s “$1.6 million annual affiliate lease” as part of the rationale for requiring Buyer consent over affiliate transactions. This expressly notes the Seller-affiliate lease arrangement in connection with the covenant, satisfying the criterion even though it does not label the rent as above-market.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies indemnification cap discrepancy (20% vs. 12.5%)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft uses a 20% cap ($43,000,000) and states that the binding term sheet requires a 12.5% cap ($26,875,000), with proposed replacement language conforming the cap accordingly.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes redline reducing cap to 12.5% / $26,875,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing the indemnification cap with $26,875,000, equal to 12.5% of the $215,000,000 base enterprise value, in the executive summary and Item 6 redline.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References the term sheet as basis for cap correction
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the $43 million/20% cap conflicts with the binding executed term sheet, which sets the general cap at 12.5% of the $215 million Base Enterprise Value ($26.875 million), and cites Executed Term Sheet §§4 and 8 as sources.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies that environmental reps survival period is too short
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft gives all non-Fundamental representations, including environmental representations, only 12 months of survival and states that this is inadequate for the target's environmental remediation and hazardous-waste business. It proposes 36-month survival for Environmental Representations and coordinates the escrow period accordingly.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Proposes extending environmental reps survival to at least 36 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes that Environmental Representations survive for 36 months post-closing in revised Section 9.01(b), and also notes the option of seeking the full applicable statute-of-limitations period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: References CERCLA/Dalton Creek exposure as rationale for longer survival
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly connects environmental exposure to longer survival. In Item 7, it argues that 12 months is inadequate because the Hargrove remediation project has 18–24 months remaining and the Dalton Creek matter may not crystallize into a formal claim for years, supporting 36-month survival for Environmental Representations. It also identifies Dalton Creek as a long-tail CERCLA exposure elsewhere in the memorandum.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies anti-sandbagging provision in Section 9.06
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 9.06 as an anti-sandbagging provision and quotes its language barring Buyer from indemnification for breaches or inaccuracies of which Buyer or its representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes replacing with pro-sandbagging language
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing Section 9.06’s anti-sandbagging provision with a pro-sandbagging clause stating that Buyer’s indemnification and other remedies are not affected, limited, diminished, or impaired by any investigation or knowledge obtained before or after execution or Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Provides actual pro-sandbagging contract text
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes actual proposed pro-sandbagging contract language in Item 9, replacing Section 9.06 and expressly providing that indemnification and other remedies are not affected by Buyer's investigation, knowledge, or notice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies need for Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek CERCLA matter
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes a separate Dalton Creek Special Environmental Indemnity in new Section 9.02(e), covering the EPA CERCLA §104(e) request and related liabilities. It also specifies separate survival, basket, cap, escrow, and direct-recovery treatment rather than relying solely on general environmental representations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity survival of 72 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the Dalton Creek Special Environmental Indemnity survives until 72 months following the Closing Date, including in proposed Section 9.04(i).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity not subject to basket or cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in proposed Section 9.04(i) that the Dalton Creek Special Environmental Indemnity is a dollar-one obligation and is not subject to the Basket Amount, Deductible, or Indemnification Cap. It also states that these losses do not count toward or reduce the general cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: References Dalton Creek liability range ($1.5M-$6M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites Dalton Creek's estimated exposure of $1.5 million to $6 million in the rationale for the Special Environmental Indemnity and includes the same range in proposed Schedule 9.02(e).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies problematic earnout operational covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 2.05's requirement to operate consistently with past practice and in good faith to maximize the earnout as overly restrictive, explains that it would constrain integration and other operational decisions, and proposes replacing it with a narrow primary-purpose anti-avoidance covenant.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes limiting earnout covenant to no-frustration standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the affirmative past-practice/maximization covenant with a narrow no-frustration standard: Buyer may not take action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the earnout. It also preserves Buyer's discretion to operate, integrate, restructure, and manage the business without affirmative operating obligations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Explains rationale — Buyer integration/restructuring flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that the Seller’s broad earnout covenant would restrict Buyer’s post-closing integration, restructuring, pricing, personnel, capital-allocation, and bolt-on strategies. It also proposes language preserving Buyer’s discretion to integrate, restructure, and otherwise manage the Company, subject only to a narrow primary-purpose restriction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies missing payoff letter requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft permits repayment “at or promptly following the Closing” and lacks a pre-closing payoff-letter requirement. It proposes delivery of executed payoff letters from each indebtedness holder at least three Business Days before closing, with lien-release commitments and simultaneous payoff through the closing funds flow.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letters at least 3 business days pre-closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed Section 2.03(d) requires executed payoff letters from each holder of Closing Indebtedness no later than three Business Days before Closing, and requires each letter to include wire instructions and commitments and documentation for lien releases, including UCC termination statements and other release instruments.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes simultaneous repayment at closing through funds flow
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the “at or promptly following” mechanic with a requirement that all Closing Indebtedness be repaid simultaneously at Closing through the funds flow, with no indebtedness remaining outstanding after Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letter delivery as a condition to closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes adding new Section 7.02(i), under Buyer’s closing conditions, requiring Buyer to have received the specified payoff letters, lien-release commitments, and wire instructions. It also states that the term sheet makes delivery a Buyer closing condition.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies missing government contract anti-assignment/novation requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft omits government-contract novation/consent protections and does not address FAR 42.12, the Anti-Assignment Act, or analogous state requirements. It proposes targeted representations, covenants, and closing conditions for federal and state government contracts, including specified US Army Corps and BLM contracts.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References specific government contracts requiring novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum specifically identifies two federal government contracts by contract number—W912DR-21-D-0045 and L23PX-00412—as requiring FAR 42.12 novation requests, corresponding to the US Army Corps of Engineers and Bureau of Land Management contracts.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Proposes closing condition or covenant for government contract novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes both a specific pre-closing covenant requiring Seller and the Company to prepare and submit government-contract novation and recognition packages and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain them, and a closing condition addressing submission, non-denial, and interim-performance approval where required.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References Anti-Assignment Act or FAR provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly references FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12 and the Anti-Assignment Act as the legal basis for government-contract novation and change-of-control requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies missing environmental permit transfer/notification covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies this gap in Item 12, noting that the Seller draft represents the Company holds 23 environmental permits but lacks a covenant addressing change-of-control notices, approvals, transfers, or post-closing cooperation. It also proposes a pre- and post-closing cooperation covenant covering notification, transfer, reissuance, amendment, and approval requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Proposes cooperation covenant for environmental permit transfers
criteria_results.reasoning: Item 12 proposes new Section 6.06A requiring pre-closing identification and submission of environmental permit change-of-control notices, applications, and approval requests, plus Seller cooperation for at least 12 months post-closing with transfers, reissuances, amendments, and approvals under applicable agency requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes that permits may require notification even in a stock deal
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the diligence memo identifies Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada environmental permit change-of-control requirements “even in a stock transaction,” and proposes notice, approval, and cooperation covenants for those permits.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies missing R&W Insurance subrogation waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies in Item 11 that the Seller draft contains no provision addressing R&W insurance or insurer subrogation rights and proposes a waiver of subrogation against Seller, subject to a fraud exception.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Proposes subrogation waiver provision with fraud exception
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 10.11 requiring the R&W insurer to waive subrogation, contribution, recourse, and related claims against Seller and its affiliates, with an express exception for claims arising from Seller's actual fraud. It also identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters as the insurer and calls for policy consistency.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: References R&W Insurance policy / Granite Ridge Underwriters
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that Whitmore is obtaining R&W insurance from Granite Ridge Underwriters and connects that policy to the need for a subrogation waiver, including proposed waiver language and a recommendation to confirm the binder and policy are consistent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (duration)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Seller draft's five-year non-compete and proposes replacing it with the term sheet's agreed three-year period, noting that the term sheet fixes the duration.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (geographic)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Seller draft’s nationwide non-compete as overbroad and proposes limiting the covenant to Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada in accordance with the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (activity)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft’s five-year nationwide restriction covering “any business” is overbroad and revises it to the term-sheet scope of environmental remediation services and hazardous waste management services.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete duration to 3 years
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly narrows the non-compete period to three years following the Closing Date, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete geographic scope to OR, WA, CA, NV
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly limits the non-compete to environmental remediation or hazardous waste management services in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete activity scope to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly limits the non-compete to businesses providing “environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services,” matching the required term-sheet scope.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Notes enforceability risk of overbroad non-compete
criteria_results.reasoning: Item 10 expressly states that the five-year, nationwide, “any business” restriction would sweep in Evergreen’s unrelated construction and timber operations and raises enforceability concerns. It also proposes carve-outs for those legitimate businesses.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification cap issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: The indemnification cap discrepancy is expressly rated High priority in both the executive summary (Item 6) and the detailed markup section, satisfying the requirement that it be Critical or High.

criteria_results.title: Anti-sandbagging issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.06's anti-sandbagging issue is expressly labeled “Priority: CRITICAL,” which is the highest tier and satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies provisions acceptable as drafted
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a dedicated Section IV, “Provisions to Leave as Drafted,” identifying the basket/deductible, knowledge qualifier, good-standing certificates, Delaware governing law, and escrow amount as acceptable, with brief explanations tying them to the playbook or term sheet.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum flags items for partner/client discussion
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a dedicated “Open Items for Partner / Client Decision” section flagging multiple issues for Elena, Marcus, and the client team to resolve before finalizing the markup, including the government-contract closing condition, environmental survival period, Dalton Creek escrow sizing and facts, and R&W insurance terms.

criteria_results.title: Escrow amount correctly stated as $16,125,000 (7.5% of EV)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum correctly states the escrow amount as $16,125,000 and identifies it as 7.5% of the $215 million base enterprise value in its indemnification discussion and no-markup summary.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Proposes 36-month escrow holdback for Special Indemnity
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly provides that the escrow portion allocated to the Dalton Creek Special Environmental Indemnity must remain available through 36 months after closing, while direct recovery continues through the 72-month survival period. It also calls for revising the escrow exhibit to reflect the 36-month Special Indemnity reserve.

criteria_results.title: Earnout maximum correctly referenced as $25,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The earnout discussion expressly states that the term sheet confirms a $25 million maximum earnout payment, correctly referencing the required $25,000,000 amount.

criteria_results.title: Earnout Adjusted EBITDA threshold correctly referenced as $38,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: In the earnout discussion, the memorandum expressly states that the term sheet confirms a $38 million full-payment Adjusted EBITDA threshold.

criteria_results.title: Earnout floor correctly referenced as $32,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The earnout discussion correctly identifies the $32,000,000 floor, the $38,000,000 full-payment threshold, and linear interpolation between them, which satisfies the pro-rata requirement.

criteria_results.title: References playbook as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the Buyer M&A Playbook as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the MAE qualifiers, earnout covenant and EBITDA adjustments, affiliate transactions, indemnification and escrow mechanics, environmental survival, special environmental indemnity, pro-sandbagging, restrictive covenants, R&W insurance, permit cooperation, and government-contract protections.

criteria_results.title: References term sheet as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the executed term sheet as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the earnout mechanics (Item 2), debt payoff mechanics (Item 5), indemnification cap and escrow (Item 6), environmental-representation survival (Item 7), Dalton Creek Special Indemnity (Item 8), restrictive covenants (Item 10), and R&W insurance subrogation waiver (Item 11).

criteria_results.title: References environmental DD memo for at least one markup position
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum repeatedly cites the Environmental DD Memo as support for markup positions, including government-contract novation provisions, environmental representation survival, the Dalton Creek special indemnity, permit change-of-control cooperation, and disclosure-schedule corrections.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies specific SPA section numbers for issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum ties well over 8 issues to specific SPA section numbers, including Sections 1.01, 2.05, 6.01, 4.16, 6.05, 7.02, 2.03, 9.04, 9.08, 9.01, 9.02, 9.06, 6.09, 4.14, and proposed new sections.

criteria_results.title: Proposed redline language is actual contract text for at least 8 issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides draft-ready contract text for well over 8 issues, including MAE qualifiers, earnout covenants and mechanics, affiliate transactions, government contracts, debt payoff, indemnification cap and escrow, environmental survival, the Dalton Creek special indemnity, pro-sandbagging, restrictive covenants, R&W insurance, and permit cooperation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness
criteria_results.reasoning: The payoff-letter markup expressly identifies all three debt holders: Cascade Mutual Bank, Pacific Lease Corp., and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. (the subordinated seller note). This exceeds the requirement to mention at least two sources or the total indebtedness figure.
